에 marks time too — 아침에 'in the morning'. 먹다's stem vowel is ㅓ, so the past is 먹었어요.

Literally 'dry the glass.' Etiquette rides along: juniors clink lower and turn slightly away to drink — M4's politeness ladder, operating at the table.
M17's nominalizer wearing M2's 도, absorbed by M7's all-purpose 괜찮아요. The gap deck's 혼밥 has made solo dining a named, normal thing — this sentence is its motto.
M4's bare 안녕 finally gets its module — and 이야 is the casual copula, 이에요 with the formality snapped off. Welcome to 반말.
The most-sent text message in Korea. Questions in 반말 need no machinery at all — drop the 요, raise the pitch, done.
-자: the let's-ending, 반말's own propositive — M9's -(으)ㅂ시다 with the tie loosened. M12's -(으)러 rides along; M18's 떡볶이 is the destination.

Said 추카해 — the ㅎ-merge the sound interlude promised. Add -요 for politeness, 합니다 for ceremony; the song uses this exact casual form.

아니다 — the negative copula you've conjugated since M4's 아니에요 — in its casual skin. 괜찮아, minus its 요, still absorbs everything.
너 — the 'you' Korean spends most of its energy avoiding — is safe here, between friends. 최고야: highest praise, lowest register.
M7's 웃다 as a bare casual command: 웃어! The full escalation available: 웃으세요 (please laugh) → 웃어 (laugh!) → silence (the joke failed).

놀다 — play as a kid, hang out as an adult, no embarrassment either way. 놀자 is the friendship imperative; the ㄹ stays put before -자.
The sentence that starts every rumor. -지 마 again — in 반말, prohibitions come in two syllables and are ignored in one.

여보세요 — phone-only, never face to face. M10's 누구 wearing M9's -세요: the politest possible 'who ARE you.'
-(으)면: the if/when hinge. Consonant stems take 으면 (있으면), vowel stems take 면 — the vowel-checking habit you've had since -(으)세요.

note: M13's 후에, M20's hinge, M22's 제일 — and the gap deck's 집 떠나면 고생이다 proverb, proven again. Every journey's real destination.

Two exhibits in one: 본 (the past badge on M1's 보다) and 어땠어요 (어떻다 in past tense). Casual speech drops the particle after 영화 — questions move fast.
The national why-deflector, straight from the gap deck's oldest resident: sometimes there is no reason, and Korean has one word for saying so politely.
The date machine's asking mode: M5's 몇 in front of 월, and its fused fossil 며칠 for the day. Big-to-small, month before day, always.

note: -는데's debut, job one — background-setting: state the situation (어제부터 온몸이 아픈데 —), then make your move inside it. The move here is the 것 같다 hedge from M34, on its noun-인 row: 몸살인 것 같아요 — self-diagnosing the overwork illness this module names. The doctor will agree; Korea always does.

Job two — soft contrast: -았/었는데 = 'I did, BUT.' M7's -지만 argues the mismatch; -는데 just notes it and waits. M10's 약 gets eaten (Korean's way since that module), M14's 아직 still means still, and M14's 낫다 shows its ㅅ-irregular past: 나 + 았 → 나았어요. The pharmacist's follow-up question is already loading.

Job three — the trailing-off -는데요…: land soft and let the listener finish. Walk up to the 약국 counter with exactly this and the pharmacist takes over — that's the design: the unfinished clause hands them the turn. M14's 목 covers throat and neck both; M9's 조금, clipped to 좀, softens; and the -는데요 ending is Korea's politest incompletion.

rom: halmeonikkeseo jinanjue susureul badeusyeonneunde naeil toewonhaseyo
note: The treatment arc, honorifically: M47's 께서 and the -(으)시- it agrees with (받으셨-) carry 할머니 from 수술 to tomorrow's 퇴원, while -는데 does its background job between the clauses. 수술을 받다: operations, like M36's 상처, are received (M9's 받다). Good news in hospital Korean sounds exactly like this.

rom: eotteon jeungsangi isseuseyo? yeori nago eojireowoyo
note: The consultation opener and its answer: M24's 어떤 asks what KIND, wearing the -(으)세요 courtesy M4 planted and M47 systematized. The reply itemizes — M14's 열 through M28's eruption-나다 (fevers COME OUT, like everything that erupts), then 어지럽다 conjugated by M11's ㅂ-family: 어지러워요. You can now give a history, not just a location.

rom: yojeum maeil undonghaeseo geongangi jeomjeom joajigo isseoyo
note: The chart, plotted upward: M35's 점점 rejoins the -아/어지다 machine it was sold with — 좋아지다, inside Ring 1's -고 있다, is improvement in progress. M8's 운동하다 takes the credit via -아/어서, and M14's 건강 collects it. The sentence every 의사 hopes to hear at the follow-up.

rom: abeojineun geongangeul wihaeseo olhae geumyeonhagiro haesseoyo
note: New Year's Korean: the -기로 하다 resolution machine (M48) locks in 금연, and M32's 위하다 aims it at M14's 건강 — the noun frame (건강을 위해서), still serving. 금연하다 is what M20's 끊다 note already did to 담배, made official. The 아버지 of this sentence has announced it to an audience; the family enforces.

en.t: I'm going to rest up properly

rom: seuteureseu ttaemune mani jichyeosseoyo. geuraeseo ibeon jumareneun puk swiryeogo haeyo
note: The burnout confession and its cure: 지치다 reports the long wear — M14's 스트레스 and M29's 때문 assign blame — then M7's 그래서 pivots to the plan, built with M50's -(으)려고 하다: M14's 푹 (doctors prescribe it verbatim) plus M8's 쉬다. Rest, intended. Whether the weekend agrees is another module.

en.t: the people who use the subway

rom: nyuseue uihamyeon jihacheoreul iyonghaneun saramdeuri neureonatdago hamnida
note: 에 의하면 debuts welded to M32's quote machine — the exact pairing M32 built with 에 따르면, one verb stiffer. 이용하다 picks its object the way PA announcements do (a service, not a thing), 이용하는 wears the -는 badge (M24), and 늘어났다고 합니다 is the shape of half of all broadcast statistics: source, claim, relay.

rom: sueop sigane hanguk munhwae gwanhaeseo iyagireul nanwosseoyo
note: 에 관해서 debuts exactly where the 에 대해서 frame (M32) taught you to stand — swap the verb, gain a register. And 이야기를 나누다 is the module's thesis in miniature: Korean conversations are SHARED, not held — 나누다 splitting cake and talk with the same verb.

rom: jeongbuga eoje josa gyeolgwareul balkyeotseumnida. ttohan saeroun gyehoekdo balpyohaetseumnida
note: The X-ray live: M13's 밝다 through M37's causative 히 — make-bright — and the metaphor never blinks: the results were dark, the government lit them. Then 또한 pivots to the second clause the way every article's second paragraph does. 합니다체 (M4) throughout, because this is a wire-service sentence; the literal lamp (불을 밝히다) waits in the word note.

rom: jeodo hanguk yeoksae gwansimeul gatge dwaesseoyo
note: M28's 가지다 note promised the squeeze — 'Spoken Korean squeezes it to 갖다' — and here it pays out, riding M35's -게 되다: the interest HAPPENED to you. 관심을 갖다 is the collocation print prefers over plain 있다 (M24's 관심 ran on the 있다-chassis): interest as a thing you hold, not just have around.

rom: dongsaengi tto munjereul ireukyeoseo jega haegyeolhaesseoyo
note: The second X-ray: M8's 일어나다 (happen) through M37's party = make-happen — 문제를 일으키다, the news collocation, here at kitchen-table scale. 해결하다 answers it in the same breath: one sibling raises what the other unties (解). Ring 1's -아/어서 chains cause to cleanup, and M29's 또 confirms this is not the first time.

rom: oneul sueobeul machigo chingudeulhago pijareul nanwo meogeosseoyo
note: M10's 수업 note ran 수업이 끝났어요; 수업을 마치고 is the same bell, one register up — and M10's -고 chains it into the evening. Then the table verb: 나눠 먹다, dividing as eating — one 피자 (M30), several hands. The formal verb and the shared meal in one breath: written Korean, spoken life.

rom: oneul achim jihacheollyeogeseo sagoga balsaenghaetseumnida. gyeongchari jigeum josahago itseumnida
note: M36's 사고 note filed 사고가 났어요 as 나다 'in its grimmest job'; 발생했습니다 is the same eruption in print — the register pair, side by side, is this module's whole thesis. Then 조사하다 takes over: M44's noun conjugated at last, running the -고 있다 progressive every breaking-news crawl runs on.

우선 opens the meeting the way M8's 먼저 opens a queue — agenda-first. 부터 (M6) picks the starting point, Ring 1's -(으)ㅂ시다 keeps it collegial, and 살펴보다 does what it was hired for: the details, together, before anyone decides anything. M44's 자료 gets its inspection at last.

en.t: I know how to drive, but

note: The know-how machine's debut: -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 = the skill is in your hands. Radar against Ring 1's very own sentence 저는 운전할 수 없어요 (M10): 수 measures whether a way exists, 줄 whether you've learned the trick — you can hold the license and still lack the 자동차 (M50). M7's -지만 files the tragedy.

en.t: I thought it would rain, but

rom: biga ol jul aranneunde nuni wasseoyo
note: 줄's second job: past-tense 줄 알았어요 flips from skill to MISTAKEN BELIEF — I thought it would rain, and the sky disagreed. M53's fresh -는데 stages the correction (알았는데 = thought-so, but…), and M11's 비/눈 pair plays both weathers. Korean files bad forecasts and unlearned skills in the same little noun.

en.t: the person who knows how to make kimchi

rom: uri baneseo gimchireul damgeul jul aneun sarameun jeoppunieyo
note: Two dependent nouns shake hands: the know-how clause wears M24's badge to modify 사람 (담글 줄 아는 사람 — note M40's 담그다 dropping its ㅡ), and 뿐 seals the census: 저뿐 = me, full stop. The ballad version runs 너뿐이야; the kimchi version is more useful and better fed.

rom: i geuncheoeneun bap meogeul dega han gundedo eopseoyo
note: 데's place-habitat with the prospective badge M25 taught inside -(으)ㄹ 때: 먹을 데 = a to-eat spot. Then 군데 counts what 데 names — the same 데 riding inside the counter — and the 도-negative frame from M29's 아무도 empties the map. The office-park lunch crisis, in one sentence.

rom: yumyeonghan sikdangeseoneun handu sigan jureul seoya dwaeyo
note: 줄's rope-sense on duty: 줄을 서다 (M14's 서다) = stand in line — the 맛집 (M18) liturgy. 한두 opens the estimate ladder: weld M5's counter-forms and 'about' comes free. Ring 1's -아야 돼요 (M10) makes the wait a law of nature, which in Korea it is.

rom: jeohui jibeneun keompyuteoga du dae isseoyo
note: Two slice words shake hands: 저희 (M4's 우리 bowed low — 'our' said to an outsider) and 대, the machine-counter M5's emergency 개 was covering for. 두 shapeshifts before its counter exactly as M5 drilled; the humility shapeshifts by audience — to your own family it's 우리 집 again.

rom: gyaeneun hangsang da aneun deusi malhaeyo
note: 걔 = 그 애 through the 준말 press (M29's pointer + M47's 애) — how friends actually say 'he'. Then 듯이 rides the badged clause: 아는 듯이 = as-if-knowing — M41's 처럼 does this for nouns, 듯이 for whole claims. Every group chat has this 걔.

터's grammar face, squeezed: 터 + 이다 + M53's -ㄴ데 = 텐데 — 'the ground truth will be that you're tired, and given that situation…'. Expectation plus the situation-setter, welded into Korean's gentlest nag. M7's 피곤하다 and M8's 쉬다 have waited fifty modules for this exact kindness.

The frame's debut: verb + -(으)ㄹ (the prospective badge you've been using since -(으)ㄹ 때, M25) + 예정입니다 = it is scheduled to. Station boards, itineraries, and wedding invitations all run on it, in 합니다체 — schedules wear suits. M8's 출발하다 supplies the course's oldest departure.

rom: geu geonmureun nopiga baek miteo jeongdoyeyo
note: The measure factory delivering: 높다 nouned to 높이, then measured on the double-subject chassis 인기가 많아요 taught you (the building's HEIGHT is the thing that equals 100m). M30's 미터 finally gets a sentence, and M32's 정도 fuzzes the number exactly as its note promised.

관리 verbs with 하다 the moment it lands, and M44's -기 위해서 aims it: in-order-to-manage. M31's 마다 schedules the regimen, M8's 운동하다 executes it. 건강 관리 is the collocation on every pharmacy poster — self-management, the national hobby.

rom: hyeonghago jeoneun ki chaiga byeollo an nayo
note: 차이가 나다: differences ERUPT through M28's 나다, the same door 화가 나다 and 기억나다 use. M17's 별로 demands its negative, as always, and M27's 키 keeps the people-height job so 높이 can keep the buildings. Fully spoken register — brothers get measured back to back.

rom: oneureun ilbuman hago nameojineun naeil haryeogo haeyo
note: The fraction trio at work: 일부 now, 나머지 later, the 전체 implied and postponed. M50's -(으)려고 하다 carries the intention, M10's -고 stitches the halves, and 만 rations the effort. Procrastination, but with precise vocabulary.

M45's -적으로 demoed 일반적으로 before the root existed for you; today the root reports and the adverb is legal. Bonus radar, live: this 길이 is M12's road wearing the subject particle — the OTHER 길이 measures trousers. M12's 막히다 does what it has done since s12.

rom: eommu siganeneun gaein jeonhwareul an badayo
note: 업무 and 개인 drawing the line every office draws: work-as-filed versus the individual. The contrast-는 (M8's oldest trick) rules the clause, M20's 전화 gets M9's 받다 refused by 안. When the door sign says 업무 중 (S2's busy-sign machine), this sentence is its policy.

대표님 — the title every startup hallway echoes with, 님 attached the way 선수 (M17) taught you titles ride names. 원래 files the backstory in one word (said 월래), and the past copula 였어요 closes the case. Office gossip register: two of today's words, zero extra grammar.

rom: busan chinguga jeonhwaro mureobwasseoyo: bap mutna?
note: The recognition frame this appendix drills: standard Korean carries the story, the dialect arrives as a quote. 밥 뭇나? is 밥 먹었나 — the -나 marks it yes/no by the fork rule — and it means what 밥 먹었어? has meant since M1: I'm checking on you. Answer in 표준어; smile in any dialect.

M32's quote machine doing exactly what it was built for: relaying speech you can hear but wouldn't produce. 단디 해라 — 단단히 pressed flat plus the plain -라 command M33 taught you to read inside quotes — is the southern grandmother's entire parenting philosophy in four syllables.

M51's 소리치다 launches the sales pitch, and two S4 words ride it: 아지매 (아줌마, southern edition) and 억수로 (intensity measured in rainfall). M3's 시장 has sounded exactly like this since Module 3 — now you can hear WHERE the stall is from.

아이가 is M42's -잖아요 in 경상 uniform — we-both-know, tagged on with a grin. M38's -(으)면서 keeps the laughing and the saying in one body, and M15's 맞다 supplies the verdict being celebrated. The most exportable sentence in the southern catalog.

M20's -(으)면 sets the standing law, and 겁나 does the intensifying — fear, worn down into WOW, exactly the path 억수로 took through rain. M31's 전라도 gains its sound; the 맛집 shows that made this word national were mostly filmed there.

M10's 대답하다 wearing M4's -(으)시- for the elder, M10's 천천히 setting the pace the stereotype expects — and 괜찮아유 meaning, per regional custom, anything from yes to no to we'll-see. The tempo is real, the ambiguity is the actual dialect.

M36's 쓰이다 holds the sign up (written-and-staying, the passive + -아/어 있다 state), M33's -게 sizes the letters, and the island's own hello does the greeting. First word of 제주어 most visitors meet; for most, the entire vocabulary of a critically endangered language, on a souvenir mug.

rom: harabeojikkeseo nongsareul jieusin ji beolsseo sasip nyeoni neomeosseoyo
note: 농사를 짓다 debuts — the collocation that completes M54's maker list — inside two Band 5 machines running at once: 께서 (M47) honors the farmer and the time-since frame -(으)ㄴ 지 (M46) counts his years. The ㅅ-irregular melts before the honorific: 짓 + 으신 = 지으신, exactly as M54 drilled.

rom: sijangeseo oihago sangchureul sanneunde aju sinseonhaesseoyo
note: The greengrocer scene, hinged on -는데 (M53): the purchase is background, the freshness is the news. 신선하다 doing its produce-aisle job on M3's 시장 run — the sentence every satisfied shopper says on the walk home.

쌀's first job is the rice-pot's first step, run on M40 machinery: 담그다 immerses (담가 — the ㅡ-drop), -아/어 두다 banks the soak for later. Between M8's 씻다 and the cooker's button lies this sentence — the quiet ritual under every bowl of 밥.

마다 (M31) sets the farm calendar, and 심다 debuts with M40's 콩 in the ground — the proverb crop, planted where beans will come up (the gap deck knows). 밭에 shows the field's soft ㅌ: 바테. The subject drops, as Korean fieldwork does — everyone knows who's planting.

rom: sagwareul an ttamyeon ttange tteoreojyeoseo sseogeo beoryeoyo
note: The orchard's verdict, delivered by -아/어 버리다 (M52): the rot is total and past helping. -(으)면 (M20) issues the warning, M36's 떨어지다 does the falling, and 따다 meets 썩다 in one cause-and-effect chain — pick on time or the tree keeps the lesson.

rom: achimeneun tomatohago danggeuneul garaseo juseureul mandeureoyo
note: 갈다's grind-sense at breakfast — the ㄹ-verb runs smooth into 갈아서, no irregular drama. The contrast-는 on 아침에는 flags mornings as the virtuous shift (M8's old topic trick), and two of the greengrocer's brightest go into the blender.

만큼 (M47) declares the amounts equal, and history agrees: the ox was the tractor, the savings account, and a family member with a name — households wept at its sale. This is the weight M56's barn proverb assumed; now you know why fixing the 외양간 late was tragedy, not carelessness.

-죠 (M51) invites agreement with the obvious — and the obvious is true: the postwar wheat pivot put 밀가루 under half the modern menu. The doubled 도 (M2's particle, twice) sweeps both carbs into one basket; (으)로 names the raw material, as it has since Ring 1.

rom: gyeoul oseun dukkeopgo yeoreum oseun yalbayo
note: The geometry law in one breath: clothes are FLAT, so they take 두껍다/얇다 — never 굵다/가늘다. The oldest connective -고 (M10) balances the pair while the contrast-는 does the seasonal bookkeeping. Say it while packing and the suitcase sorts itself.

Raindrops are ROUND, so growing rain 굵어져요 — 굵다 riding the -아/어지다 becoming-machine (M35), with -(으)니까 (M10) drawing the conclusion. 펴다 opens M9's 우산 the way it opens books and backs. English rain gets heavy; Korean rain gets thick.

rom: achime angaega jiteoseo api jal an boyeosseoyo
note: 짙다 on home turf — M49's 안개 finally gets its proper adjective. The passive party's 보이다 (M36) reports what reached the eye: 안 보였어요, nothing did. Calibrate the dial as you drive: fog is 짙다, never 진하다 — density, not strength.

rom: i keopineun saegeun jinhande maseun yeonhaeyo
note: Both knobs of the intensity dial in one cup: 진하다 up, 연하다 down, hinged on the -는데 contrast M53 formalized. The doubled contrast-는 (색은... 맛은) is the course's oldest trick doing precision work. Reviews of hand-drip cafés read exactly like this.

M51's 월드컵 note put 'entire cities in red shirts' on the record; now you can SAY it — 붉다 wearing the badge, welded to 색 by the M7 rule that builds every color noun. 온 (M55) spreads the red over the whole 도시 (M22). The shirts belong to the 붉은 악마 — the Red Devils; the vocab note holds the name.

rom: abeojikkeseo geoul apeseo nektaireul maego gyeseyo
note: 매다 lands on the tie M21 dressed with the all-purpose 넥타이를 해요 — the knot finally has its own verb. 께서 (M47) lifts the subject and 계시다 (M4) lifts the progressive to match: honorifics agree end to end. 거울 (M13) frames the morning scene.

조각 on counter duty — 한 조각 of M19's 케이크 — inside the 밖에+negative frame M39 drilled: nothing-but-one-piece not-remains. 남다 (M35) files the leftovers. English says 'only one left'; the Korean grammar performs the scarcity.

rom: aideuri jongireul jeobeoseo jageun baereul mandeureosseoyo
note: 접다's debut, and a radar going live: this 배 is the BOAT — the third career M3's 배 note filed ('also pear and boat'). 종이 (M15) folds into 종이접기 territory, and -아서 chains the folding to the launching. Fleet-building remains a rainy-day national pastime.

The title culture in one hallway: the vocative 과장님 — never a bare name, per the law M16's 부장님 note laid down ('always with 님') — then 께서 (M47) because the 부장님 outranks everyone in earshot, and the verb agreeing through -(으)시- (M4). Rank is grammar here: one sentence, three honorific systems, zero names.

rom: seonbaega babeul samyeon hubaeneun keopireul sayo
note: The rank choreography, catered: entry date decides who pays bigger — the 선배 covers the meal, the 후배 answers with coffee, and -(으)면 (M20) files the custom as a standing law. Seniority is expensive by design; juniors repay it later, downward, to 후배 of their own.

rom: hanguk namjaneun botong daehaksaeng ttae gundaee gayo
note: The factual sentence under a thousand dramas: conscription interrupts most degrees midway — M27's 군인 note counted the ~18 months. 대학생 때 (때, M25) timestamps it; 보통 (M8) makes it statistics, not destiny. 군대에 가요 states it the way Korea does: no drama, total consequence.

rom: sinipsaeng ttaeneun modeun ge saerowonneunde beolsseo joreopsaengi dwaesseoyo
note: -는데 (M53) hinges freshman nostalgia to the graduating present, and 새롭다 (M35 — 'new-to-the-heart') is exactly the freshman feeling. 신입생 and 졸업생 bookend the -생 economy the way 입학/졸업 (M44) bookended the paperwork; 벌써 (M23) does what 벌써 always does — arrives too soon.

rom: yojeum jeolmeunideureun gongmuwoni doeryeogo yeolsimhi siheomeul junbihaeyo
note: -(으)려고 (M50) aims a generation: the 공무원 시험 is Korea's stability lottery, complete with prep towns and repeat years. 요즘 젊은이들은 is the eternal editorial opener — now you can read the op-ed AND sit the exam it worries about. 되다 (M10) plus intention: become, on purpose.

Every call center's opening liturgy, word for word: 고객님 first — the ROLE honored, no name needed — then 잠시 (M29, the formal moment) wearing 만 (M30), then the request machinery -아/어 주세요 (M9). Dial any service line in Korea and this sentence answers back.

rom: uri ban banjangeun moksoriga jeil keoyo
note: The double-subject frame Korean measures people with — the possession chassis of 인기가 많아요 (M17): the 반장 owns a voice, the voice owns the superlative (제일, M22). 반장 = 반 (M15) + chief-長: the ladder's first rung, elected by classmates and enforced by lungs.

rom: i munjeneun jeonmungahante mureoboneun ge jokesseoyo

rom: eojjeoda boni mudaeeseo noraereul bureuge dwaesseoyo
note: 어쩌다 보니 (gap deck) opens the story every Korean tells about their own life, and M35's -게 되다 closes it: circumstances did this, not planning. Between them, M51's 무대 hosts. The two machines together are the national humble-brag — nothing was intended, everything happened.

rom: uri halmeonineun dongneeseo gimchi baksarago bullyeoyo
note: The naming frame: M32's quote-라고 + 불리다 = is-called-X, how titles get pinned on people. M44's 박사 note licensed the honorary use — any impressive know-it-all — and M36's passive 리 turns M19's 부르다 around: the neighborhood does the calling; 할머니 just receives the crown.

rom: jyeotjiman uri timeun majimakkkaji choeseoneul dahaesseoyo
note: M39's 최선 note called 최선을 다하다 'the sentence that closes exams, interviews, and this band' — today the verb inside it finally gets its own card. -지만 (Ring 1) concedes the scoreboard to M17's 지다; 다하다 keeps the receipt: effort fully spent, with M15's 마지막 as the finish line.

rom: noraebangeseo sorireul jireumyeon ssain seuteureseuga pullyeoyo
note: The module's stress cycle in one sentence: 쌓이다 piles it (wearing M24's badge — 쌓인), M36's 풀리다 unties it, and 소리를 지르다 is the folk remedy in between. M20's -(으)면 writes the prescription; M17's 노래방 fills it nightly.

rom: dongsaengi gapjagi yeohaeng iyagireul kkeonaeseo nollasseoyo
note: 이야기를 꺼내다 = bring it up — the take-out verb's conversational second job: topics get pulled from pockets like wallets. M28's 갑자기 does the timing, and Ring 1's -아서 hands the surprise downstream to M26's 놀라다. The dropped subject of the second clause is you, mid-sip.

rom: chuun gyeouri jinago ttatteuthan bomi chajawasseoyo

The 되다-tail in its natural register: the swap-the-하다 machine (M36) on a frozen parent (진행하다 = conduct), announcing that things are under way. M54's 대로 measures reality against M8's 계획, and Ring 1's -고 있다 keeps the verb running. Read it in the voice of a wedding MC.

en.t: I'm about to go out of my mind

note: 미치다's second life, calibrated for the office: M49's -겠- makes the madness imminent rather than achieved — 미치겠어요 = I'm ABOUT to lose it, which is exactly the distance that keeps it sayable to coworkers. Ring 1's -아서 supplies the cause. The reach-sense stays in the newspapers; this sense does the sweating.

rom: jibe mak dochakhaesseul ttae dongsaengi gwajareul mak meokgo isseosseoyo
note: 막's two dictionary rows in one house: 막 도착했을 때 (M25's -(으)ㄹ 때 catching the moment) is the just-now 막; 막 먹고 있었어요 is 마구 clipped — no aim, no napkin. Same syllable, sorted entirely by its neighbor: an arrival makes it timing, a mess makes it manner.

en.t: And as luck would have it,

rom: jangmaga machimnae geuchyeosseoyo. machim oneureun geuri deopjido anneyo
note: The timing pair, calibrated live: M35's 마침내 releases what was long awaited (M11's 장마, finally 그치다-ed); 마침 credits the lucky coincidence that followed. Then 그리 measures the heat downward with its mandatory negative, and M26's -네요 notices it in real time. Three adverbs, three different clocks.

rom: sijangeseo gwaireul jantteuk saseo naengjanggoreul gadeuk chaewosseoyo
note: The quantity set calibrating itself mid-errand: 잔뜩 loads the arms, 가득 tops off the container. M37's 채우다 — whose note decoded the be-full verb 차다 hiding inside it — does the filling, and M13's 냉장고 receives. One shopping trip, two different fullnesses.

rom: nuni waseo sesangi ontong hayaeyo. olhae gyeoureun yunanhi chuun geot gatayo
note: 온통 paints M22's 세상 edge to edge — M49's 하얗다 keeping its ㅑ in 하얘요, exactly as its note drilled — and 유난히 upgrades the weather smalltalk with M34's hedge riding shotgun. Two new adverbs doing what this module promises: same sentence you could always build, now tuned.

en.t: The second our friend opened the door,

rom: urineun saengil patireul mollae junbihae noasseoyo. chinguga muneul yeoljamaja kkamjjak nollago mucheok joahaesseoyo
note: The manner corner throws a party: 몰래 keeps the secret, M40's -아/어 놓다 banks the preparations, M38's -자마자 times the door, and 깜짝 놀라다 lands the collocation M26's 놀라다 note rehearsed ('깜짝 is the jump itself'). 무척 closes it on the feelings beat, where it lives.

rom: bunmyeonghi usaneul gabange neoeo dwonneunde jigeum eopseoyo
note: 분명히 pays the debt M34's 분명하다 note wrote ('분명히 봤어요 = I DEFINITELY saw it'): eyewitness certainty, sworn. M40's -아/어 두다 filed the umbrella away; M53's -는데 sets up the betrayal. The more 분명히 a Korean sentence starts with, the more missing the umbrella turns out to be.

rom: yeok gakkaie saraseo hoesakkaji gyeou sip bunbakke an geollyeoyo
note: 가까이 in its noun calling — 역 가까이에 = in the station's near, the second job the list grants it — and 겨우 belittling the commute with M39's 밖에 co-signing the smallness. M12's 걸리다 takes the time; there's barely any to take. The apartment listing writes this exact brag.

rom: maeil daneoreul jeogeodo yeol gaessik oeumyeon sillyeogi jogeumssik joajyeoyo
note: 적어도 sets the negotiator's floor — M7's 적다 through M39's even-if machine, 'even at its fewest' — and M43's 씩 doses it per day. 조금씩 delivers the payoff M43's deck made folklore (조금씩 저축하세요), aimed at M26's 실력 instead of the bank. This app's entire business plan, in one conditional.

잘못하다's confession, in the order Korean gives it: fault first, feeling second. One rung below M4's apology pair — 미안해요 regrets, 잘못했어요 ADMITS. Kids deliver it with both hands raised; adults deliver it when regret alone won't cover the bill.

rom: neomu geokjeonghaji maseyo. da jaldoel geoyeyo
note: The blessing, finally legal: M10's 잘 and 되다 fused into 잘되다 and sent into the future -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (M8), while -지 마세요 (M14) clears the worry first — M14's own 걱정하다 doing the worrying. Said before exams, interviews, and surgeries: Korean optimism is grammar-shaped.

rom: han beoneun silsujiman du beoneun jalmosieyo
note: The calibration, run as arithmetic: M5's numbers count M12's 번, and -지만 (M7) draws the line. A 실수 slips once and gets a laugh; repeat it with the warning in hand and it becomes 잘못, which owes an apology. M16's deck confessed 실수했어요 long ago — today the noun takes the stand.

잘못되다 behind a triple hedge: M24's badge freezes the damage (잘못된), the seems-machine (M34) declines to swear to it, and the trailing -는데요 softener (M53) leaves the sentence open for the listener to fix things. Blame the address (M12's 주소), never the person — Korean customer service in one line.

Textbook Korean's stage direction — the line printed above half of all exercises. 알맞다 wears M24's badge, M34's 고르다 does the picking (the market version was 골라 골라!), and S2's among-중 locates the candidates: 다음 중에서 = from among the following. M15's 답 has waited since Ring 1 to be chosen this properly.

바르다's second job on its first day: M10's 약 spread onto M36's 상처, on the -기 전에 timer (M13). The same verb that keeps your posture 바른 keeps the wound medicated — uprightness and ointment share one spelling, and the pharmacist doesn't blink.

그중에서 opens the superlative frame M22 built for 제일, and 강하다 debuts in the Sino suit — M16's 팀, graded. Radar in the stands: M41's 세다 flexes native muscle (힘이 세다); 강하다 rates teams, signals, and coffee. The 強 rode frozen through M56's 강조하다; today it plays.

소용없다 closes the door that the -아/어도 concession (M39) opens: the tears are granted — cry away (M7's 울다) — and the outcome still doesn't move. Blunter than 괜찮아요: not 'it's okay' but 'it won't help.' Said by parents at toy-store exits nationwide.

rom: jeoneun sincheongeul deungnokhago jechulhamyeon hwagini doego bogoga jeondaldwaeyo.
note: The application axis, run as one long verb chain: 신청 → 등록 → 제출 → 확인 (the noun) → 전달 — the five steps you now own. The -고 chaining (M10) hands each step to the next, and -면 (M20) gates the last two: file, register, submit, it comes through, it gets relayed. M6's 은행 sits at the far end of the counter, waiting for the whole chain.

rom: hoesaga myeongnyeonghago gyuchigi heoyonghago jehanhaneunde neomeumyeon wibani dwaeyo.
note: The rule ladder, rung by rung: the firm (M2's 회사) hands down a 명령, the rule (M39's 규칙) lets it through (허용하다), the 제한 (limit) is set — and M36's 넘다 draws the line. Cross it and the 위반 (breach) fires, with M10's 되다 sealing the verdict. One axis: command → permission → cap → breach.

rom: sinyongi joeumyeon eunhaengi kadeu sincheongeul heoyonghaeyo.
note: 허용하다 meets the bank: M6's 은행 is the institution that says yes (here to M9's 카드), and it runs purely on 신용 — credit, the thin line between being trusted and being turned away. M1's 좋다 sets the bar, and -면 (M20) gates the whole thing: good credit, then the card.

rom: geullojaga seontaegeul gwonhago kadeureul yocheonghaeseo hoeuie chamseokhaeyo.
note: The worker's day, three bureaucratic verbs in a row: the choice (선택, the noun over M33's 선택하다) gets advised (권하다 — radar: not M5's 권, the 'right/book'), the card (M9's 카드) gets requested (요청), and M10's 회의 gets the attendance (참석하다). The -고 chain (M10) links the first two verbs; -해서 folds the request into the reason for showing up.

The meeting machine: 논의 (the discussion) runs to its end — M8's 끝나다 doing the ending — and then M10's 회의 moves forward (진행하다) with the choice. -면 (M20) hands it off: once the talking is done, the institution executes the decision. It's the same choice (선택) the worker was advised on — now it's the meeting's move.

en.t: puts the worker to the work,

rom: daegieobi geullojareul hwaldongsikimyeon cheongnyeonege gyeongheomi ssayeoyo.
note: The firm's investment in its people: 대기업 (the big firm) puts the worker (근로자) to the work (활동하다, M3's 시키다 forming the causative 활동시키다), and the youth (청년) — the people who will carry the firm's name — let the experience (M33's 경험) pile up. M61's 쌓이다 does the stacking on its own; the experience is the subject and the person takes 에게. You don't collect experience — you do work, and it piles up on you.

rom: hoesaga ingureul bogohago cheongnyeonui yocheongeul jeondalhaeyo.
note: The firm's two reporting jobs: the population (인구) is reported (보고 — the noun, the report you hand up), and the youth's (청년의) request (요청) is relayed (전달). M2's 회사 does the work, and M43's 보고서 is the paper form of the same 보고. One verb — 전달 — bridges the two clauses: you report a number and you pass on a want. The -고 chain (M10) glues the two jobs to the same doer.

rom: jeongbuga gyoryureul heoyonghamyeon gyoryuro sinyongi ssayeoyo.
note: Diplomacy, run as arithmetic: the government (M32's 정부) permits the exchange (교류) — the flow of people and goods — and the credit (신용, the same 신용 the bank runs on) stacks up (M61's 쌓이다). M6's -로 marks the means: not by force, by trade. A nation's 신용 is built the same way a person's is, by letting things flow through.

en.t: wake in the inner room in the morning,

rom: jeoneun achime anbangeseo ireonago bokdoreul geotgo hyeongwaneuro gayo.
note: The room tour, run as one walking chain: the inner room (안방, this module's heaviest room) sets the wake, the corridor (복도) carries the walk, and the entryway (현관, M13's 현관) is the go-to. M6's 걷다 and M1's 가다 do the moving; -고 (M10) hands each step to the next and -으로 marks the destination. The whole sentence stays inside the house — every room, one axis.

rom: sillaeeneun sopaga itgo, wijjok changmuneun bakkwieosseoyo.
note: The interior as a single volume (실내, 室 inside) holding a sofa (M13's 소파), and the upper-side window (위쪽 + M6's 창문) freshly replaced. M1's 있다 pins the sofa in place; M35's 바뀌다 is the renovation the window went through.

rom: mulsogeneun mulgogiga itgo, kkumsogeneun chinguga isseoyo.
note: The X-inside factory applied twice: the fish (물고기, M22's 물고기) swims in the inside of water (물, M1's 물), and the friend (친구, M1's 친구) appears in the inside of the dream (꿈, M8's 꿈). The same 속 gives a body and a mind the same kind of inside; M28's 속 is the factory, M1's 있다 is the verb that puts something in each.

rom: seulpeumeun gaseumsoge itgo, geokjeongeun meoritsoge isseoyo.
note: The feeling-organs of the X-inside factory: 슬픔 (M42's 슬픔) lands in the chest's insides (가슴, M30's 가슴 + 속), and 걱정 (M29's 걱정) runs on in the head's insides (머리, M8's 머리 + 속). Same 속, two organs, two feelings.

rom: changbakkeul bomyeon nunapi neolgo, apgireul georeobomyeon bakkachi boyeoyo.
note: The outside as seen, not as touched: the window-outside (창밖, this module's look-through-the-glass) measured with M1's 보다, the eye-front (눈앞, M14's 눈 + M6's 앞) judged wide (M13's 넓다), the road-ahead (앞길, M6's 앞 + M12's 길) given a try on foot (M6's 걷다 riding M16's -아/어 보다 try-machine), and finally 바깥 (the outside as a place) coming into view on its own (M36's 보이다).

en.t: a sound comes out of the neighboring house.

note: The next-door pair, built the same way: 옆방 is the room on the next side (M6's 옆 + M8's 방), 옆집 the house on the next side (M6's 옆 + M1's 집). M13's 조용하다 holds the quiet on one side; M19's 소리 rides M28's 나다 across the wall from the other. Quiet and loud share one axis.

en.t: and the school gate connects to the campus center.

rom: gangdang muni yeolligo, gyomungwa kaempeoseu senteoga tonghaeyo.
note: The school's gates, run as openings: the hall (강당, 講+堂) is the school's big room; its door (M6's 문) opens on its own (M36's 열리다); and the school-gate and the campus center (교문 + 캠퍼스 + 센터) connect (M32's 통하다) — the way a campus is one connected ground.

en.t: The firm's branch is at the front-side corner,
the main gate's door closes in the evening.

rom: hoesa jijeomi apjjok koneoe itgo, jeongmun churimmuneun jeonyeoge dathyeoyo.
note: The firm's two doors: the branch (지점 — 支 branch-off + 店 shop, this slice's one C-grade word) sits at the front-side corner (앞쪽 + 코너), pinned there by M1's 있다; the main gate (정문, 正+門) has its entrance door (출입문) close on its own (M36's 닫히다) when the evening (M2's 저녁) comes. Same 정 sound, two different hanja — 正 the main, not M26's 정 the feeling.

en.t: point at the fish with my finger,
and the friend points at the river.

rom: jeoneun songarageuro mulgogireul garikigo, chinguneun gangeul garikyeoyo.
note: The pointing finger (손가락, M28's 손가락) out, tip leading, the target named by direction. M22's 물고기 (fish) is what the finger says, and the river (M22's 강) is what the friend names. 가리키다 (point at) does both — the M66 pointing-finger verb used twice, at the small thing and the big one.

rom: appaga keobe mureul butgo, mureul heullyeoyo.
note: The pour-and-spread axis in one breath: M4's 아빠 (dad) tips M1's 물 (water) over the lip of M18's 컵 (cup), and the same water leaves its glass by accident. 붓다 (pour) is the liquid-pour verb, 흘리다 (spill) the thin run-out — the two pour-verbs of the module at the same cup, and 흘리다 is just M35's 흐르다 (flow) with a hand on it: the flow, caused.

The run-and-chase axis, welded to M1's go/come verbs: M17's 달리다 (run) in its -어 coat gives 달려가다 (run to), and M32's 따르다 (follow) in its -어 coat gives 따라가다 (follow along). M1's 친구 runs toward M22's 강 and I run one step behind.

en.t: If my friend gives the ball,

note: The give-back compound doing the round trip: 돌려 (turning back) + M9's 주다 (give) makes 돌려주다 (give back). M25's 아기 (baby) receives M17's 공 (ball) from M1's 친구 (friend) and hands it right back — the two M9 give-verbs, one forward one return, with -(으)면 (M20) gating the trade.

en.t: pick up the ball with my finger,

rom: jeoneun songarageuro gongeul jipgo, gongeul jjilleoyo.
note: The fingers-act family on one ball: the thumb and two fingers close on M17's 공 (ball) with 집다 (pick up) and M28's 손가락 (finger), and the same hand goes sharp with 찌르다 (poke) — the tip leading, the point against the ball. Two finger-verbs, one soft one sharp, on the same thing — and 찌르다 is 르-family (M7): 찔러요.

The burst-and-drop axis, both causative: M36's 터지다 with the -뜨리다 tail makes M17's 공 (ball) burst — 터뜨리다 — and M36's 떨어지다 with the same tail makes M18's 컵 (cup) fall — 떨어뜨리다. The two burst/fall verbs you met in M36, now with a hand behind them.

en.t: stomps it, and knocks on the door.

rom: agiga gongeul chago, gongeul balgo, muneul dudeuryeoyo.
note: The foot-verbs running the full range on M17's 공 (ball): M25's 아기 (baby) swings the foot with 차다 (kick) — M14's 발 (foot) leading — then comes down on it with the heavier 밟다 (stomp on), and lands the fist flat on M6's 문 (door) with 두드리다 (knock). Three foot-and-fist verbs of the module, one kick one step one knock.

en.t: shake out my hair, and rest my hand on the book.

ko.t: 머리를 털고, 손을 책 위에 얹어요.

rom: jeoneun chaegeul dwijipgo, meorireul teolgo, soneul chaek wie eonjeoyo.
note: The turn-and-layer axis on one shelf: the front face of M1's 책 (book) goes over to the back with 뒤집다 (flip) — M6's 뒤 (back) + 집다 (pick up) — then M8's 머리 (hair) gets shaken out with 털다 (shake off), and M8's 손 (hand) comes to rest on top with 얹다 (put on top). Three turn-and-layer verbs: one flip, one shake, one rest.

The factory's rule in the wild: his 기쁘다 is invisible; his 기뻐하다 you can film. M41's 처럼 does the simile, M9's 받다 hands over the trigger, and -고 (M10) strings receipt to reaction. To report someone ELSE's feeling in Korean, describe the performance.

rom: eodum sogeseoneun jageun sorido keuge deullyeoyo
note: 어둠's debut in its natural habitat — M28's 속: the -(으)ㅁ freezer made a PLACE out of an adjective. M36's 들리다 (the passive party) reports what ears receive rather than what they do, and 크게 is 크다 through the -게 adverbializer (M33). Turn off the lights and the grammar goes passive with you.

rom: i noraereul deureumyeon yennal chinguga saenggangnayo
note: 생각나다 needs no effort, only a trigger — the song opens M28's 나다-door and the friend walks through uninvited. -(으)면 (M20) sets the tripwire, and 듣다 (M2) shows its ㄷ-irregular colors: 들으면. Notice who the subject is: the FRIEND arrives; you do nothing.

rom: nuneul gamgo gohyang jibeul tteoollyeo boseyo
note: The triangle's third corner, on command: 떠오르다 (M49) floats up on its own; the causative party (M37) hands you the crane — 떠올리다, you MAKE it float into 머릿속 (M65). 감다 (M41) closes the eyes and the try-machine (M16) makes it an invitation. Meditation apps run entirely on this sentence.

en.t: I had such a scary dream that

rom: eoje bame museoun kkumeul kkwoseo jameul mot jasseoyo
note: The doubled object, twice in one breath: 꿈을 꾸다 dreams a dream, 잠을 자다 sleeps a sleep — M28's 잠 note said Korean doubles up happily, and here is the proof running back to back. M24's 무섭다 wears the badge; -아/어서 chains cause to casualty.

The national alarm phrase: a big matter just erupted through M28's 나다 — the same door memories and feelings use, now admitting a crisis. 잃어버리다 (M20) supplies the finality its 버리다 tail always promised. Shout 큰일 났어요 and every Korean within earshot turns around.

웬일이에요 asks for no facts — it performs the double-take. The visit itself is the answer; the pleasure is the point. Its information-seeking cousin is 무슨 일이에요? (M10's 무슨): one investigates, the other celebrates. File this under greetings, not questions.

rom: himdeureodo aideuri useul ttae borameul neukkyeoyo
note: The teacher's credo, fully machined: -아/어도 (M39) concedes the 고생, -(으)ㄹ 때 (M25) marks the payoff moment, and 보람 — the felt worth English has no word for — arrives through 느끼다 (M32): 보람을 느끼다 is THE collocation. 힘들다 (M15) drops its subject the way natural Korean does.

rom: chinguneun je iyagireul deureumyeonseo gogaereul kkeudeogyeosseoyo
note: The nod, live: 고개를 끄덕이다 with its polite contraction on display — 끄덕였어요, never 끄덕이었어요. M38's -(으)면서 runs the listening and the nodding in parallel, which is exactly how Korean agreement works: on the beat, while you talk. M2's 듣다 shows its ㄷ-irregular on the way in — 들으면서.

-지 마세요 from M14, aimed at the module's bluntest gaze: held eye contact is a challenge or a crush, and either way the watched party feels it. M34's 부끄럽다 explains itself through M42's -잖아요 — you KNOW it's embarrassing — while M33's 그렇게 measures the manner. The politest possible way to say stop looking at me.

rom: san wieseo dosireul naeryeodabomyeon geokjeongi jaga boyeoyo
note: 내려다보다 doing its literal job from M11's 산 — M22's 오르다 got you up here — with M20's -(으)면 drawing the payoff and M36's 보이다 reporting how things LOOK rather than how they are. Perspective as grammar: climb, look down, and M29's 걱정 shrinks on its own.

rom: jega ireumeul bulleonneunde chinguneun geunyang doraseoseo ga beoryeosseoyo
note: 돌아서다's whole drama in one motion: M53's -는데 sets the scene and drops the 'but,' then M52's -아/어 버리다 closes the door — 가 버렸어요: gone, nothing to be done. M19's 부르다 shows its 르-shape (불렀-). The turned back says more than the mouth ever did.

The 뛰어- squadron's maiden flight on M66's chassis — the same weld as 달려가다, other engine: M28's 뛰다 + M8's 나가다. M38's -자마자 clocks the zero-second gap between M8's 끝나다 and the stampede through M6's 밖. Every classroom in the country empties exactly like this.

rom: cheoeum mannasseul ttae urineun maju seoseo aksureul haesseoyo
note: 마주 puts M14's 서다 front-to-front and 악수하다 seals it — 오른손, remember, 왼손 in support if respect is due. M25's -(으)ㄹ 때 frames the moment, and M15's 처음 note already filed the spoken half of this ritual (처음 뵙겠습니다); this is the body half. Bow, shake, or — Korean default — both at once.

다가가다 pays M50's IOU — 다가오다's note promised the mirror that approaches away from you, and here it is, aimed at M25's 아기 with M10's 천천히 doing the caution. M28's 잡다 lands on its oldest collocation, 손을 잡다. Approach is a verb you conjugate carefully around small humans.

The flag-ceremony posture: 올려놓다 lifts the grid's first cell onto M30's 가슴, M10's -고 chains the gesture to the song, and M19's 부르다 sings it — 노래를 부르다, its note's own collocation. Body language formal enough to have a national protocol; the rom shows the ㅎ-merge live: 올려놓고 says 올려노코.

rom: jeol madange oraedoen tabi itgo, seunimi geu apeseo gidohago gyeseyo
note: The temple set assembles on M26's 절 — whose note promised 'context bows to context'; here context says building. M54's 마당 holds the 탑, M35's 오래되다 wears M24's badge to describe it, and the 스님 prays inside Ring 1's progressive with M4's 계시다 swapped in — the respect and the grammar rising together.

en.t: Every time she goes to the temple,

rom: halmeonikkeseoneun jeore gasil ttaemada gajogui geongangeul biseyo
note: M47's 께서 honors the subject while M25's -(으)ㄹ 때 and M31's 마다 stack into 가실 때마다 — every single visit. Then 빌다 shows its ㄹ-stem manners: the ㄹ bows out before ㅅ, so the honored wish is 비세요, not 빌으세요. What she asks for never changes; M14's 건강 is the Korean grandmother's entire portfolio.

rom: daeum ju siheom ttaemune doseogwaneseo chaegeul daseot gwonina billyeosseoyo
